_help: Inputs for The Ages' Grand Timeline (lessons/humanities/the-ages.html, #grand-timeline). Milestones only: the turning points a student should be able to place, one or two per big idea, each linked to the lesson that teaches it. Lesson timelines keep their detail; add an event here only if it belongs on the one-line story of everything. `npm run build:ages-timeline` merges these with The Ages' artifact data (artifacts and faithArtifacts in the page script, which also drive the 3D viewer) and writes the list into the page; `npm test` fails if the page is stale, a date won't parse, or a lesson link is missing. Dates use timeline.js syntax (see CLAUDE.md); traditional or uncertain dates are marked c. `strand` must be a key of `colors`.

eras.label: Middle Ages
eras.text: Not a "Dark Age": monasteries, translation houses, universities, cathedrals and trade networks kept and grew knowledge across Europe, the Islamic world, Africa and Asia.

eras.label: Renaissance
eras.text: Recovered classical learning, perspective in art, and new patrons and printers bridge the medieval world to the Scientific Age.

Jesus.label: Life of Jesus
Jesus.text: Jesus of Nazareth teaches, heals and is crucified in Roman Judea; his followers proclaim the resurrection.

Paul's letters.label: Paul's letters
Paul's letters.text: Paul writes to young churches across the Roman world; his letters are the earliest Christian writings we have.

Edict of Milan.label: Edict of Milan
Edict of Milan.text: Constantine and Licinius grant Christians legal toleration in the Roman Empire.

Nicaea.label: Council of Nicaea
Nicaea.text: Bishops from across the empire meet and produce the first form of the Nicene Creed.

Great Schism.label: Great Schism
Great Schism.text: The churches of Rome and Constantinople formally divide into Catholic West and Orthodox East.

Printing Bible.label: Gutenberg Bible
Printing Bible.text: The first major book printed with movable metal type in Europe.

Reformation.label: Reformation begins
Reformation.text: Martin Luther's 95 Theses spread by print and start the Protestant Reformation.

Global church.label: A global church
Global church.text: Christianity's center of gravity shifts south: most Christians now live in Africa, Latin America and Asia.

events.label: Big Bang
events.text: The universe begins hot and dense and starts expanding; its afterglow is still visible as the cosmic microwave background.

events.label: Sun and planets form
events.text: A collapsing cloud of gas and dust forms the Sun; the leftover disk builds the planets.

events.label: Earth forms
events.text: Earth gathers from colliding rock; the Moon likely forms soon after from a giant impact.

events.label: LUCA: life's common ancestor
events.text: Every living thing traces back to one population of simple cells, roughly 4 billion years ago.

events.label: Cambrian explosion
events.text: Most major animal body plans appear in the fossil record within a few tens of millions of years.

events.label: First forests
events.text: Woody trees spread across the land, changing soils, climate and the air.

events.label: Coal forests
events.text: Carboniferous swamp forests are buried and slowly become most of the world's coal.

events.label: Pangaea
events.text: Nearly all land is joined in one supercontinent before it rifts apart into today's continents.

events.label: Dinosaurs' extinction
events.text: The Chicxulub impact (with Deccan volcanism) ends the age of non-avian dinosaurs.

events.label: Ice Age peak
events.text: Ice sheets cover much of North America and Europe; sea level is about 120 m lower than today.

events.label: Counting on bones
events.text: Notched tally bones show people recording numbers long before writing.

events.label: The wheel
events.text: Wheels appear in Mesopotamia and Europe, first for pottery and then for carts.

events.label: Writing and base-60 numbers
events.text: Sumerian scribes keep accounts in cuneiform and count in sixties, which is why an hour has 60 minutes.

events.label: Pythagoras
events.text: The Pythagoreans link numbers to shapes and to musical harmony.

events.label: Plato's Republic
events.text: Plato's allegory of the cave asks what it means to see the truth.

events.label: The Appian Way
events.text: Rome begins its first great paved road; roads tie the empire together.

events.label: Euclid's Elements
events.text: Proof-based geometry and number theory, including infinitely many primes; taught for 2,000 years.

events.label: Archimedes
events.text: Archimedes explains buoyancy and levers and traps pi between two polygons.

events.label: Eratosthenes measures the Earth
events.text: Shadows in two Egyptian cities give Earth's circumference with remarkable accuracy.

events.label: Antikythera mechanism
events.text: A Greek bronze gear computer predicts eclipses and planetary positions.

events.label: Zero becomes a number
events.text: Brahmagupta writes rules for calculating with zero and negative numbers.

events.label: Fibonacci's Liber Abaci
events.text: Hindu-Arabic numerals reach Europe, along with the rabbit puzzle behind the Fibonacci sequence.

events.label: Dante's Divine Comedy
events.text: Dante's journey through Inferno, Purgatory and Paradise is written in Italian, not Latin.

events.label: Leonardo's Mona Lisa
events.text: Leonardo da Vinci works on the Mona Lisa while filling notebooks with machines and anatomy.

events.label: Raphael's School of Athens
events.text: Raphael paints the great thinkers of Greece together in the Vatican.

events.label: Copernicus puts the Sun at the center
events.text: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres moves Earth out of the middle of the universe.

events.label: Tycho Brahe's new star
events.text: A supernova shows the heavens can change; Tycho's measurements become the best before the telescope.

events.label: Kepler's laws
events.text: Kepler shows planets move in ellipses; Galileo turns a telescope to the sky the same year.

events.label: Milton's Paradise Lost
events.text: Milton's epic retells the fall in blank verse.

events.label: Newton splits light
events.text: Newton's prism experiments show white light is a mixture of colors.

events.label: Newton's Principia
events.text: The laws of motion and universal gravitation explain falling apples and orbiting moons alike.

events.label: First copyright law
events.text: Britain's Statute of Anne gives authors, not printers, the right to copy their work.

events.label: Bach's Brandenburg Concertos
events.text: Bach dedicates six concertos to the Margrave of Brandenburg.

events.label: Vivaldi's Four Seasons
events.text: Four violin concertos paint spring, summer, autumn and winter in sound.

events.label: Linnaeus names and ranks life
events.text: Systema Naturae sorts living things into nested groups; later editions give every species a two-part name.

events.label: Euler and e
events.text: Euler calculates e to 18 digits and makes it a central number of mathematics.

events.label: Franklin's kite
events.text: Benjamin Franklin shows lightning is electricity.

events.label: Watt's steam engine
events.text: James Watt's separate condenser makes steam engines efficient enough to power the Industrial Age.

events.label: Mozart's Magic Flute
events.text: The Magic Flute premieres weeks before Mozart dies, leaving his Requiem unfinished.

events.label: Lewis and Clark
events.text: The Corps of Discovery maps a route across North America to the Pacific.

events.label: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony
events.text: Beethoven, almost completely deaf, premieres the symphony with the Ode to Joy.

events.label: Hokusai's Great Wave
events.text: Hokusai's woodblock print becomes one of the most recognized images in art.

events.label: Faraday's induction
events.text: A moving magnet makes electric current: the principle behind every generator.

events.label: Ada Lovelace's program
events.text: Lovelace's Note G sets out an algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine: the first published program.

events.label: California Gold Rush
events.text: Gold at Sutter's Mill draws some 300,000 people to California.

events.label: Darwin's Origin of Species
events.text: Darwin explains how natural selection shapes living things over generations.

events.label: Maxwell's equations
events.text: Maxwell unites electricity, magnetism and light in one theory.

events.label: Mendel's peas
events.text: Gregor Mendel publishes the rules of inheritance from his pea experiments.

events.label: Mendeleev's periodic table
events.text: Mendeleev arranges the elements and leaves gaps for elements not yet found.

events.label: Brooklyn Bridge opens
events.text: Emily Roebling sees her family's bridge through to completion; she is the first to cross it.

events.label: Tesla's AC motor
events.text: Tesla patents the AC induction motor, and alternating current goes on to power the world.

events.label: Van Gogh's Starry Night
events.text: Van Gogh paints the view from his window at Saint-Rémy.

events.label: Curie discovers polonium and radium
events.text: Marie and Pierre Curie find two new elements and name radioactivity.

events.label: Joplin's Maple Leaf Rag
events.text: The best-selling rag makes Scott Joplin the King of Ragtime.

events.label: Quantum physics begins
events.text: Max Planck proposes that energy comes in tiny packets, or quanta.

events.label: First Nobel Prizes
events.text: Alfred Nobel's will funds prizes for physics, chemistry, medicine, literature and peace.

events.label: Wright brothers fly
events.text: The first powered, controlled airplane flight lasts 12 seconds at Kitty Hawk.

events.label: Einstein's miracle year
events.text: Special relativity, E = mc², and light quanta in a single year.

events.label: Ford's moving assembly line
events.text: Henry Ford's line cuts the time to build a Model T from hours to about 90 minutes.

events.label: Panama Canal opens
events.text: Locks lift ships across Panama, linking the Atlantic and Pacific.

events.label: Einstein's general relativity
events.text: Gravity is the curving of space and time.

events.label: Penicillin
events.text: Alexander Fleming notices mold killing bacteria: the first antibiotic.

events.label: The universe is expanding
events.text: Hubble shows distant galaxies are moving away from us.

events.label: Turing's universal machine
events.text: Alan Turing describes a machine that can compute anything computable.

events.label: Snow White
events.text: Disney's first full-length animated feature.

events.label: Tolkien's The Hobbit
events.text: Middle-earth begins; The Lord of the Rings follows in 1954–55.

events.label: Hedy Lamarr's frequency hopping
events.text: Lamarr and George Antheil patent the idea behind today's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.

events.label: Breaking Enigma
events.text: Codebreakers at Bletchley Park read German Enigma messages during World War II.

events.label: The transistor
events.text: Bell Labs builds the transistor, the switch inside every chip.

events.label: The Turing test
events.text: Turing asks: can a machine imitate a human in conversation?

events.label: Grace Hopper's compiler
events.text: A-0 lets programmers write instructions closer to English.

events.label: DNA's double helix
events.text: Watson, Crick, Franklin and Wilkins reveal how DNA stores genetic information.

events.label: The perceptron
events.text: Frank Rosenblatt's learning machine is the ancestor of today's neural networks.

events.label: ELIZA
events.text: Joseph Weizenbaum's chatbot shows how easily people read minds into machines.

events.label: Apollo 11 lands on the Moon
events.text: Armstrong and Aldrin walk on the Moon, guided by software led by Margaret Hamilton.

events.label: Sesame Street
events.text: Jim Henson's Muppets help teach a generation to read and count.

events.label: Apple is founded
events.text: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak start Apple in a garage; personal computers follow.

events.label: Pale Blue Dot
events.text: Voyager 1 photographs Earth from 6 billion km away.

events.label: Python is released
events.text: Guido van Rossum releases Python, now one of the world's most-used languages.

events.label: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
events.text: A computer defeats the world chess champion in a match.

events.label: Steve Jobs unveils the iPhone
events.text: A phone, iPod and internet communicator in one device puts computers in everyone's pocket.

events.label: Higgs boson found
events.text: CERN confirms the last missing particle of the Standard Model.

events.label: CRISPR gene editing
events.text: Doudna and Charpentier show CRISPR can cut DNA at a chosen spot.

events.label: AlphaGo beats Lee Sedol
events.text: A learning program wins at Go, a game long thought too intuitive for computers.

events.label: First image of a black hole
events.text: The Event Horizon Telescope photographs the black hole in galaxy M87.

events.label: King David
events.text: David unites Israel's tribes and makes Jerusalem the capital.

events.label: Solomon's Temple
events.text: Solomon builds the first Temple in Jerusalem.

events.label: Jerusalem falls to Babylon
events.text: Babylon destroys Jerusalem and the Temple (often dated 587/586 BC); the exile begins.

events.label: Cyrus takes Babylon
events.text: Persia conquers Babylon and lets exiled peoples, Judeans among them, return home.

events.label: The Septuagint
events.text: Jewish scholars in Alexandria begin translating the Hebrew Scriptures into Greek.

events.label: Second Temple destroyed
events.text: Roman legions destroy Jerusalem's Temple.

events.label: King James Bible
events.text: The Authorized Version shapes English Bible reading for centuries.
